turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): alright, vitals first. blood pressure is 148 over 92, pulse 96, temperature 37.2 celsius, oxygen 99 percent, respirations 18. urine dip just now, umm, large blood, leukocytes negative, nitrites negative.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): hey, I'm Dr. Shah. rough one?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): yeah. this pain in my left side came on all of a sudden last night. that's why I'm here. I can't sit still.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): pacing the hallway at like two. I thought he threw his back out at work.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): not my back. it started around two, in the loin under the ribs, and it shoots down into the groin. left side. feels like something ripped.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): score it for me, zero to ten?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): uh a seven. well actually it jumps around, seven to nine. call it a really bad eight.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): any vomiting?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): once. only once, around four. bile, I think. I'm still queasy though.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): blood in the urine too?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): yes. pink, cola colored, and the next one was still a little pink. my uncle had bladder cancer and I can't stop thinking that's this.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): I get the spiral. colic with blood is a stone far more than a tumor. any burning when you pee?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): no. no burning. does a stone even burn? sorry.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): often no. any fever or chills?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): no. I wasn't hot. no chills.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): chest and breathing, that system, anything going on?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): no. breathing's normal. chest is fine.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): diarrhea? constipation?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): no, bowels are fine. normal this morning.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): kidney stone before?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): no. never.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): what medicines are you on?
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): lisinopril, 20 milligrams every morning, for his blood pressure. I fill the pill box, so.
[SEG0024] person_1 (NURSE): uh the chart says lisinpril 10 mg daily. March med rec.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): that list is wrong. I'm on 20. every single morning.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): chart says 10, you both say 20. I won't guess a dose. blood pressure problem is ongoing?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): yeah, about five years. oh and I took Tylenol around 4, two extra strength, 500 each, so a thousand milligrams. nothing. I don't take ibuprofen.
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): wait, did the Tylenol spoil the urine dip? I feel like I messed the whole visit up.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): no, acetaminophen doesn't cover up blood or a stone. belly's soft, no guarding. left flank is tender right where you jumped. right flank is not tender.
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): ow. so one night of this, is the kidney already hurt? am I headed for surgery today?

[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): thinking it through out loud. pain from the loin to the groin, one vomit, blood you saw, the dip loaded with blood, left flank tender, no fever. working impression is a left ureteral stone. provisional, the scan is what decides.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): okay. what if it's stuck though. I know I keep asking.

[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): most of these pass, and a single night doesn't scar a kidney. bloods are booked this morning, a CBC and a basic metabolic panel. the nurse draws them in a few minutes before you leave the room, no fasting.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): non-contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis, booked today at 2. no dye. don't fast, just drink a couple glasses of water before you go down.
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): good, no dye, I wouldn't even know if I was allergic to it. we just wait here until 2?
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): you wait, we walk you over. if the creatinine comes back high or the CT is equivocal, then we add a renal ultrasound. I'm not ordering that unless one of those happens.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): is a culture part of today? I don't want an infection missed. sorry.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): not today. if the white count is high, then we add a urine culture. only in that case.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): and the pain medicine is booked. oxycodone 5 milligrams by mouth, one tablet now, before the scan.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): oxycodone, that's the narcotic, right? one tablet isn't gonna addict me? can I drive after?
[SEG0041] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm driving anyway. truck's at the shop. groceries can wait, obviously.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): one tablet will not get you addicted. no driving today. if you vomit the pill back up, then we give a shot instead, and only if that happens.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): what about food and water and work? I do construction, ladders and all. am I off the whole week?
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): eat regular meals. drink two or three liters today, strain your urine, and no driving and no ladders while the oxycodone is in you.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll see you Friday morning in clinic, in three days, and we'll go through the results.
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): what if tonight gets bad, or I can't pee at all?
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): if the pain gets worse tonight or you can't pee or you keep vomiting, come to the ER. don't wait for Friday.
[SEG0048] person_3 (PATIENT): lisinopril tomorrow morning, I still take the 20?
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): yes, keep taking it as you have been. bring the bottle Friday so we settle the milligrams. we skipped allergies and a pile of other history, and that's fine for today.

spec.situation: Sudden severe loin pain going to the groin overnight, vomiting once, blood in urine; pain score given loosely; urine dip result read aloud; painkiller and scan planned today.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
